title: Introduce RAG contract sign-on walkthrough and compact quickstart
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Added a new RAG developer walkthrough covering contract-based tool signing, a compact quickstart, and an example notebook. No breaking changes.
description:
Context and motivation: Customers building agent/tool-calling flows frequently ask for a lightweight, auditable pattern for establishing and validating tool contracts when a retrieval-augmented agent needs to sign or handshake with downstream tools (e.g., vector db write hooks, webhook sinks, or secure connectors). The goal of this PR is to add a focused developer guide and compact quickstart that demonstrates a contract-first sign-on pattern for RAG agents: 1) define tool contracts (input/output schema + auth envelope); 2) generate a signed token; 3) perform a lightweight verification step inside the tool adapter; 4) run an end-to-end quickstart that exercises streaming, tool-calling, and telemetry assertions.

Summary of changes:
- docs/rag-contracts/signon.md: new step-by-step walkthrough with code snippets and diagrams, covers threat model and recommended KMS/HMAC patterns.
- examples/rag-signon-quickstart/README.md: compact quickstart with Docker devcontainer and env.example.
- examples/rag-signon-quickstart/server/index.ts: minimal tool adapter that verifies signed contract headers and emits structured events.
- examples/rag-signon-quickstart/client/sample-run.sh: scripted run that seeds a tiny index, runs the agent against the adapter, and prints step assertions.
- notebooks/rag-signon-demo.ipynb: exploratory notebook used for internal smoke testing and reproducible examples.
- docs/snippets/tool-contract-schema.yaml: canonical schema example used in the walkthrough.
- docs/sidebars.js: docsite nav update to surface the new walkthrough under "RAG -> Security & Contracts".
- tests/integration/rag-signon-smoke.test.ts: CI smoke test to exercise the Docker quickstart and ensure the contract handshake completes under CI env.

Commits (summary):
- 8c0a21a: add signon walkthrough draft and schema snippets
- 9f1d3b2: add quickstart scaffold and devcontainer
- 4b7e5c0: implement adapter verification and sample-run script
- a5d9f11: add notebook and update docs sidebar

Changed areas (high-level):
- New doc pages and site nav entry; small edits to the security and telemetry pages to reference the walkthrough.
- Small example application in examples/rag-signon-quickstart (TS + shell script); intentionally tiny to keep on-ramp low friction.
- One new CI job that pulls the quickstart Docker image and runs the smoke test in sequence.

Implementation notes:
- Signing pattern uses HMAC-SHA256 with an example KMS env var pattern (docs warn against copying exact values to production).
- Adapter verification is intentionally permissive in the example (time-window check + signature) and includes inline comments showing how to harden for production (replay protection, nonce storage, rotated keys).
- Telemetry: quickstart emits structured events compatible with the Console ingestion schema; the smoke test asserts presence of at least one "tool.contract.verified" event.

Review convo (excerpt):
- Alex Kim (review): "Nice focused guide — one ask: can we avoid including ascii art diagrams in the doc since our docsite renderer compresses them poorly? Suggest switching to a simple PNG + alt text."
- Priya (author): "Agree — replaced inline ascii with optimized PNG and added alt text. Also moved the threat-model table into a collapsible admonition so it doesn't push down the page."
- Sasha (review): "Integration test timing flaked locally — increased timeouts and added retry logic to the smoke runner. Can we also add a note about CI secrets required?"
- Priya: "Added CI secrets section to README and updated the smoke test to exit cleanly if secrets are not present (test is then skipped in CI)."
- Diego (approval): "Approach looks good for a first pass; please monitor community feedback and we can iterate on the hardening section."

CI summary:
- GitHub Actions: docs-build (pass), lint (pass), examples-smoke (pass), integration (pass). The examples-smoke job pulls the example image, runs the sample-run.sh script, collects structured events, and checks for the verification event.

Testing notes:
- Local developer flow documented in README: start the adapter (npm start), seed the index (provided script), run the agent using the local dev key.
- Notebook provides playable cells to step through token generation and signature verification with small vectors.

Security and compliance notes:
- The walkthrough explicitly calls out where customers must use customer-managed KMS or HSM for production keys.
- The example uses ephemeral keys and an explicit "DO NOT COPY" placeholder.

Accessibility and docs quality:
- New page includes plain-language intro, TL;DR code block, and an end-of-page checklist to make adoption easier for engineers.
- Sidebars updated and a short redirect added so legacy links to "security/rag-auth" map to the new walkthrough.

Merge decision: squash merge on green CI after approvals.

Post-merge tasks:
- Monitor docs feedback channel for questions and typo fixes.
- Create a follow-up ticket (ENG-1528) to add a hardened server example showing nonce storage and replay detection.
- Add example to the Quickstart gallery on the docs home page if community uptake is positive.

Why this is different from existing quickstarts: Prior RAG quickstarts focus on orchestration, replay, or local authoring. This walkthrough centers on a contract-first sign-on pattern for tool-calling with a short, auditable example and explicit production hardening guidance — aimed at teams integrating with third-party connectors that require authenticated tool calls.
